subject: Kestrel Analytics — transient inference failures and elevated P95
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@kestrel-analytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.in>
Cc: ops+redwood@kestrel-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate and slow tail on hosted inference (Kestrel)

Hi Evelyn,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx responses and increased P95 for text-generation calls to your hosted endpoint (model: rwd-3-small) around 07:45 PDT. Failure rate peaked at ~9% and P95 climbed from ~320ms to ~1.8s for a 30-minute window. This is impacting our real-time annotation pipeline.

Attached is a small snippet of errors and a screenshot of our Grafana panel. Can you confirm if there's an ongoing incident on your side or if we should investigate client-side?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Site Reliability Lead, Kestrel Analytics

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.in>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@kestrel-analytics.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and slow tail on hosted inference (Kestrel)

Hi Samira — thanks for the report and the screenshots, sorry for the impact. I'm opening an incident and escalating to our infra team now.

What we're doing immediately:
- Publishing a brief advisory to status page (link below)
- Investigating throttles, queueing, and cache behavior for the rwd-3-small fleet serving your account
- Will update every 30 minutes or sooner with findings/mitigation steps

Status page: https://status.redwood.in/incident/2027-03-12-kestrel-high-p95

I'll keep you posted here and via the ops address.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.in>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.in>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.in>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.in>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and slow tail on hosted inference (Kestrel)

Eve/Team — I'm looking at the host telemetry and request traces. Quick notes:
- Around 07:40 we see a change in cache hit ratios for prefix cache on the rwd-3-small pool servicing us-west-2; hit rate dropped from ~92% to ~35%
- Observed increased time spent on KV cache misses and a small uptick in worker queue backlog (not CPU/GPU exhaustion)
- A configuration change from earlier today adjusted the prefix-eviction threshold for the global cache (rollout completed 07:38) — suspecting aggressive eviction/TTL interaction caused many cold KV fetches

Immediate mitigation plan:
1) Temporarily revert the prefix eviction threshold to previous value (rollback in progress)
2) Increase autoscale buffer for we-west-2 rwd-3-small pool for the next 30 minutes
3) Enable more verbose tracing for failed requests to capture stack and cache keys (will attach logs)

I'm rolling the rollback now and will report back as soon as it's done.

- Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: incident_snapshot_log.txt
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.in>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@kestrel-analytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.in>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.in>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and slow tail on hosted inference (Kestrel)

Hi Samira — quick update for you: rollback completed at 08:54 PDT and we've already seen request success rate climb back to normal and P95 drop toward baseline.

What we observed after rollback:
- Hit ratio recovered to ~89% within 6 minutes
- Error rate dropped under 0.8% by 08:58 PDT
- No customer-facing config changes left in the queue

We'll keep heightened monitoring for two hours and perform a controlled canary of the updated eviction threshold with instrumentation and smaller ramp. I'll follow up with a short postmortem draft later today.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.in>

Subject: Re: High error rate and slow tail on hosted inference (Kestrel)

Samira — following up to confirm service is stable from our side. We published a short advisory to status and will post the full postmortem once it's complete (target: 2027-03-15).

Status page summary (public):
- Incident start: 2027-03-12 07:38 PDT
- Mitigation: rollback of prefix eviction threshold completed 2027-03-12 08:54 PDT
- Impact: elevated P95 and transient 5xx responses to hosted generation for ~75 minutes; customer-facing error rate peak ~9%
- Current status: mitigated, monitoring

If your team needs logs or a short runbook for client-side retries/timeouts, tell me the preferred format and I'll send them. Appreciate the quick heads-up and patience while we investigated.

Best,
Evelyn
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.in>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.in>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.in>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.in>, Samira Khan <samira.k@kestrel-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident notes and next steps (Kestrel incident)

Hi all — sharing a brief technical summary and proposed follow-ups for the postmortem: 

Root cause (preliminary): a misconfigured rollout changed the prefix eviction threshold on the shared KV cache. This caused a large fraction of requests to miss warm prefixes and trigger KV backfills, increasing end-to-end tail latency and exposing backpressure in request workers.

Immediate corrective actions taken:
- Rolled back the threshold (08:54 PDT)
- Temporarily increased autoscale buffer for the rwd-3-small pool
- Added more granular tracing for cache misses and request correlation IDs

Planned follow-ups:
- Controlled canary of the new threshold with tighter ramp and per-customer circuit (scheduled 2027-03-16)
- Hardening: add deployment gate that validates hit-rate telemetry before global rollout (owner: eng-infra, ETA 4w)
- Postmortem doc with timeline, graphs, and remediation actions (owner: Marcus, draft by 2027-03-15)

Samira — we'll share the postmortem and a short API client retry guidance note. If you'd like a quick bridge for the postmortem review, happy to set one up.

Thanks for your patience — apologies again for the disruption.

- Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
